name: April
summary: April is two different months joined in the middle: an Easter fortnight that runs at peak crowds and peak prices at both resorts, and a back half that is one of the better-value windows of the year before summer arrives.

verdict.short: Avoid the fortnight bracketing Easter and April becomes a good month, with warm weather, moderate crowds and Orlando prices stepping back down. Inside that fortnight it is as bad as July.
bestFor: The last week or ten days of the month, which is the quiet before summer at both resorts
Warm-weather rides, since Orlando's water attractions are reliably comfortable now
Universal Hollywood outside the Easter week, which holds moderate midweek crowds
Anyone catching the end of Mardi Gras at Universal Orlando
Longer daylight, with park hours extending noticeably from the winter schedule
worstFor: The fortnight around Easter, which is peak in every measure at both resorts
Southern California trips during Easter week, when local districts break together
Anyone sensitive to humidity, which begins its climb in Orlando in the second half
Budget travellers booking late, since the Easter fortnight sells out early
Visitors expecting a seasonal overlay, because there is no substantial one at either resort

crowds.shape: April's crowd shape is decided by one date, and everything else is downstream of it. The fortnight bracketing Easter runs at genuine peak at both resorts: it is the last national break before summer, it draws heavily from the northeast and from Latin America into Orlando, and unlike March's staggered breaks it concentrates almost everybody into the same ten days. Universal Orlando sees its highest non-summer attendance of the year across that window. Hollywood, which shrugs off March, does not shrug off this one — Southern California districts overwhelmingly attach their spring break to Easter, so the local base that keeps the park moderate in March is off school and in the park. Outside that fortnight, April behaves like a good shoulder month. The first week and the last ten days both run moderate at both resorts, Orlando hotel rates fall back from the peak, and the weather is still on the right side of the summer humidity curve. The other April effect is operating hours: both resorts extend them meaningfully this month, which spreads a given crowd over more usable hours than March delivered.
peakWindows: The week before and the week after Easter, at both resorts
Easter Sunday itself and the weekend around it, the busiest non-summer days of the year in Orlando
Weekends at Universal Hollywood throughout the month, on the local pass base
quietWindows: The last week to ten days, once every district is back at school
The first few days of the month in years when Easter falls late
Midweek mornings at Islands of Adventure, which opens its queues more slowly than the other two Orlando parks

universal-orlando.note: Climate normals for Orlando, not a forecast. The driest month of the Orlando year and one of the two or three most pleasant, with mid-80s afternoons and comfortable mornings. Humidity starts to build in the last third of the month, which is the first hint of what June onward is like, and the water rides at Islands of Adventure become a reward rather than a risk.

universal-hollywood.note: Climate normals for the San Fernando Valley around Universal City, not a forecast. The wet season is effectively over and the summer heat has not arrived: mid-70s afternoons, cool evenings, and three rain days in the month. On the raw numbers this is the best park weather Universal Studios Hollywood gets all year.

cost.note: April is priced as two months rather than one. The Easter fortnight carries top-tier ticket dates, peak Orlando hotel rates and the highest Express Pass prices of the first half of the year, and it sells out earlier than any other spring window because the dates are fixed and everybody knows them. Outside it, pricing falls back to something close to March's level and then drops further in the final week, which is genuinely good value: warm weather, moderate crowds, and rates that have not yet turned over to summer. The Hollywood pattern is the same shape with a smaller amplitude, because the park's one-day ticket tiers move less than Orlando's multi-day pricing does. The practical instruction is the same at both: price two candidate weeks before you book either, and expect the gap across the Easter boundary to be larger than any other decision you make in this month.

planningNotes.heading: Find Easter first, then plan everything else around it
body: Easter moves between late March and late April, and where it falls determines whether this is a good month or a bad one. Look it up before you look at anything else, because it is the only variable in April that is both knowable a year ahead and worth more than every tactic combined.

The rule that follows is simple: book outside the fortnight that brackets it. The week before is nearly as busy as the week after, because European and Latin American school breaks do not align with the US one, and Orlando gets both.

If the Easter week is the only week you have, treat it as a peak trip. That means booking the hotel early, buying Express Pass, arriving before opening every day, and planning fewer parks than you would in a quiet month rather than more.

planningNotes.heading: The last ten days are the best-value window of the spring
body: Once every district is back at school, late April at Universal Orlando delivers moderate crowds, extended operating hours, warm dry weather and prices below the March average. That combination does not recur until the second half of September, and September carries hurricane risk that April does not.

The weather argument is the strongest part of it. April is Orlando's driest month, which means the afternoon thunderstorm that shapes every summer day has not started, and a full day outdoors is comfortable in a way it will not be again until November.

The one thing missing is seasonal content. Mardi Gras is finishing, the summer programme has not started, and there is no substantial overlay at either resort. If atmosphere is what you are buying rather than rides, this is not your month.

planningNotes.heading: Hollywood loses its March advantage this month
body: The reason Universal Studios Hollywood stays calm in March is that Southern California schools do not break in March. In April they do, and they break together around Easter, so the park's Easter week runs at a level it does not reach again until the middle of summer.

That flips the coast recommendation for one fortnight. In March, California is the calmer choice; during Easter week, both coasts are bad and Orlando at least has three parks to distribute the crowd across. A compact single park under peak local demand is a specific kind of unpleasant.

Outside that week, April is close to Universal Studios Hollywood's best month on the weather alone. Mid-70s afternoons on a park built across two levels and a long escalator run is worth more here than at any flat park.

planningNotes.heading: Mardi Gras ends this month, and the exact night is not published far ahead
body: Universal Orlando's Mardi Gras has finished in late March in most cycles and has run into April in some recent ones, so whether an April trip catches it at all is genuinely uncertain rather than a matter of picking the right week. The closing date is published per cycle and has moved between years.

If the concerts are the reason for the trip, treat April as unreliable and book February or March instead. If they are a bonus, check the operator's own calendar a month out and adjust which nights you spend at Universal Studios Florida.

The parade and street party are included with regular admission, so catching them costs nothing beyond being in the right park on the right evening. That makes them worth building an evening around and not worth building a trip around this late in the season.

freshness.sourceNote: Crowd and cost shapes describe multi-year patterns at both resorts rather than a forecast for any single April. Weather figures are climate normals for Orlando and for the San Fernando Valley and do not decay. Easter moves between late March and late April, so this page describes its effect as a window relative to the holiday rather than naming dates, and the Mardi Gras closing date has moved across recent cycles.
